solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Get to assemble

definitions.meaning: to get something in the sense of understanding it, as in 'I get it'
to assemble is to come or bring together in one place

explanation.walkthrough: 'to' simply links the two definitions; 'I get it' and 'I gather' both mean I understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: one can grasp or infer a point, and people can congregate or collect together.

clue.text: Ashamed to opt for stewing such food

indicators.note: stewing ingredients get churned about, so these three words are cooked up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone embarrassed to choose a casserole of some dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stewing' rearranges the letters of ASHAMED TO OPT; 'for' is a link and 'such food' points back at the stew picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Mashed spuds are a staple side dish, so they are an example of food.

clue.text: Second group found in ruins can be little monkeys

indicators.note: found in tells us one piece sits inside the other word

parts.note: to ruin something is to mar it, so ruins gives mars
a mo is a short moment, a second
a set is a group or collection

explanation.surface: A second group discovered in ruined buildings might be small primates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' reads as an ordinal and 'ruins' as a noun for derelict buildings; 'found in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small South American primates, tiny long-tailed tree-dwelling monkeys.

clue.text: Hot — moved quietly North

parts.note: to steal somewhere is to move stealthily, past tense stole

explanation.surface: Something hot crept away northward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' is slang for stolen goods, not temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang usage: goods described as hot have been taken illegally by thieves.

clue.text: Such philosophers exalt sin — it is set to explode

indicators.note: blowing up scatters the pieces, so the letters of the five words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Philosophers who glorify wrongdoing are about to blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is part of the fodder, not the indicator: EXALT SIN IT IS SET are the fifteen letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Sartre's school of thought, which stresses individual freedom, are philosophers of that kind.

clue.text: Building society's first to support proposition

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: a premise is a proposition on which an argument rests

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A building society's leading member backs a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building society' looks like a lender; it splits into the definition and the source of S, placed below PREMISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Premises means a building with its land, as in business premises.

clue.text: Identification mark keeping one inside a Russian forest

indicators.note: keeping ... inside means one piece holds the other within it
inside completes the instruction that the numeral goes within the label

parts.note: a tag is a label used to identify something
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An identifying mark with a single item inside a Russian woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: The taiga is the vast coniferous woodland belt of Siberia and northern Russia.

clue.text: Pick up a weapon and receive the applause

parts.note: to pick something up is to take it
a bow is a weapon for shooting arrows

explanation.surface: Grab a weapon, then accept the cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: performers bend forward to acknowledge an ovation from the audience.

clue.text: Centre of fashion also known as a dance

indicators.note: centre of takes the middle letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The heart of fashion, otherwise called a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: FASHION has seven letters, so its centre is the fourth, H.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional Maori war dance, famously performed by New Zealand rugby teams before matches.

clue.text: They may help mountaineers with choices of water

indicators.note: picks of water puts the frozen water first, before the choices

parts.note: ice is frozen water
picks are choices, as in 'take your pick'

explanation.surface: Climbers' aids come with a selection of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'choices of water' reads backwards into the answer: ICE then PICKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers use these sharp-pointed axes to grip frozen slopes.

clue.text: Pretend bullets regularly going missing from mess

parts.note: a sham is a pretence, something fake

indicators.note: every other letter of the word drops out, keeping the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th

explanation.surface: Fake ammunition periodically disappearing from the army canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly going missing' drops U, L, T from BULLETS, leaving BLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene of chaos or total disorder is a mess.

clue.text: Book is first-class — a source of hope

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI

indicators.note: source of takes the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A top-rate book brings hope.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a traditional mark of excellence, from the ship register, rendered in letters as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophetic book of the Old Testament, named after the prophet.

clue.text: Frontmen feel bitter surrounded by heartless looks

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the feeling piece inside the other
heartless removes the central letter of the word

parts.note: to peer is to look closely, so looks gives peers
to resent something is to feel bitter about it

explanation.surface: Lead singers resent being surrounded by cold stares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle E of the looks word, leaving PERS; 'looks' is a verb here, not appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Television hosts who front programmes are figures at the front of a show.

clue.text: Left nothing for time in unoccupied use

indicators.note: for signals that one thing replaces another
in tells us the swap happens within the following word

parts.note: unoccupied means empty
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Leaving nothing to spare when time is unused.
explanation.walkthrough: In EMPTY, the T is swapped for L and O.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ a tool or method is to make use of it.

clue.text: Crime confined to attendant's residence

indicators.note: confined to puts the crime inside the other word

parts.note: a page is an attendant, as at a wedding
arson, deliberately setting fire, is a crime

explanation.surface: A crime restricted to a servant's dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attendant's' reads as possessive but just supplies PAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar's official house is a residence provided by the church.

clue.text: Skilled but very worried suitor has nothing

indicators.note: worried suggests being agitated, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: O resembles zero

explanation.surface: Accomplished, yet the anxious wooer has nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges the wooer's letters as IRTUOS; 'but' and 'has' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a highly skilled performer; used as an adjective it means masterly.

clue.text: Expressions of disapproval surrounding socially acceptable skirts

indicators.note: surrounding puts the abbreviation inside the noises

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval
U means upper-class, socially acceptable, in British usage

explanation.surface: Tutting around respectable dresses.
explanation.walkthrough: U, as in 'U and non-U', is old British slang for upper-class and proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Short stiff frilly skirts worn by ballerinas.

clue.text: Count on chap who sells on credit

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on top of another comes first

parts.note: to tally is to count
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: Rely on a fellow who lets you pay later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count on' reads as the idiom for relying on someone; here 'on' only places one piece above the other in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a tallyman was a salesman collecting payments in instalments.

clue.text: Back providing new seat for the party

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: providing means if, as in 'providing it rains'

indicators.note: new indicates a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Supporting a new chair for the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns IF into FI; 'new' rearranges SEAT as ESTA. 'for the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival or celebration in Spanish-speaking countries is a party.

clue.text: The bosses phrased lie deceptively

indicators.note: deceptively suggests twisting, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Management phrased a lie in a misleading way.
explanation.definitionFit: Leadership can be a collective term for the people in charge.

clue.text: EU money once key to unionist party

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
a do is a party

explanation.surface: European currency once a key to a unionist political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The former currency of Portugal before the euro.

clue.text: One's covering trade standards

indicators.note: covering means the outer piece wraps around the other

parts.note: One's gives I (one) plus S
a deal is a trade

explanation.surface: Each one handles trade standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are principles or values to aim for, standards of conduct.

clue.text: She starts to fish from promenade

indicators.note: starts takes the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: to troll is to fish by trailing a line

explanation.surface: She sets off fishing off the seafront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'from' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To promenade is to walk leisurely, to take a stroll.

clue.text: Bird finding use for one in oil

indicators.note: for signals a replacement of one letter
in shows where the swap takes place

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A bird discovers a use for oil.
explanation.walkthrough: In OIL, I (one) is replaced by USE. 'finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the blackbird, also the water bird called the dipper.

clue.text: Popular scene played out with daughter getting angry

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: played out suggests acted in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A popular scene acted with the daughter becoming furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played out' rearranges SCENE as CENSE. 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Incensed means made extremely angry, enraged.

clue.text: Tot covered in ice-cream finally panics and eats

indicators.note: covered in puts the addition inside the dessert

parts.note: a cone is an ice-cream cornet
to tot up is to add, a sum

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A toddler covered in ice-cream eventually panics and eats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' is not a toddler but a sum, as in 'tot up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food is to eat it.

clue.text: Source of genuinely ancient metal

indicators.note: source of takes the first letter of the next word

parts.note: ancient means old

explanation.surface: The origin of truly old metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious yellow element, Au, is a metal.

clue.text: One without roots lets no girl on if dressed

indicators.note: dressed suggests rearranging or arranging the letters anew

explanation.surface: A rootless drifter allows no girl on if she is clothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' rearranges LETS NO GIRL ON; 'if' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: From the proverb about moss: a rolling stone is a person who never settles.
